# RayNu-V SKU card — Shipment 1 and the final SKU

**Status:** living card. The list behind it is [ADR-021](adr/ADR-021.md) **Catalog**; this page does not carry its own list.  
**Audience:** the person who would sign, and the person who would compare us to ESXi, Proxmox or Hyper-V.  
**Public:** [`site/sku.html`](../site/sku.html) renders [`site/sku.json`](../site/sku.json), generated by `./tools/sync-sku-site.sh` from the ADR. CI runs `--check`.

Two shipments, one catalog. Every capability a professional operator expects from a PowerEdge hypervisor is a row in ADR-021 with one of three words: **lived** (printed on the R640, with a commit SHA or iron marker), **in flight** (code under iron test), or **planned** (named, not built). **Shipment 1** is the subset marked `S1`. The **final SKU** is every row. Nothing else is the product. Counts are not a score; the distance tracker stays [`docs/hda.md`](hda.md).

---

## Today's box, before either shipment

If you signed a non-production **dedicated-box** letter today, this is what you would hold, stated the way diligence would state it:

- One `r640-hypervisor.efi` on one PowerEdge R640. Ubuntu 26.04 has reached `vikkp@raynusrv2` on a 10 GiB tail of RAYNU-SPARE (`c3a70e62`).
- The disk that comes back after a chassis power-off is an **8 GiB** USB window (`928d6224`), not the array.
- The page is TLS 1.2 with a lab millicert (`RAYNU-V-M8-TLS-OK`). The first minutes of boot are still **plaintext HTTP**.
- The door is a **lab latch** (`raynu-v-bringup`) until ESP `EFI/RayNu/auth.token` exists. There is no operator account.
- The guest NIC transmits; its uplink (LOM port 4, `:39`) had no link on the lab box. **No packet has yet returned to the guest.**
- **not PERC** fleet: the rest of the 2.9 TB VD stays hidden; leave UBUNTU0 alone. **not cluster.** **not Windows.** Not a remote desktop; iDRAC is the console.

| Row | State | Why it is on the card |
|-----|-------|------------------------|
| A1 Everest | DONE | The install loop you could point at (`f72b4276`). |
| A2 Persist | DONE on evidence | Force Off, then the **8 GiB** USB window comes back (`928d6224`). |
| A3 This SKU card | **DONE** | This page, now the Shipment 1 / final SKU card over ADR-021. |
| A4 TLS | **DONE** on COM2 `928d6224` | Lab millicert. PRE-EBS SNP stays **plaintext HTTP**. |
| A5 Auth | Host-ready, not iron | **lab latch** until ESP `auth.token`. |
| A6 Console | Typed once, not a desktop | The page reached Alpine once. Ubuntu login is COM2. |

## Shipment 1 — the dedicated-box letter

One `r640-hypervisor.efi`, signed, booted from iDRAC virtual media or USB on a PowerEdge R640. The operator reaches an HTTPS page with their own certificate and their own account, on a management port with a static address they chose. They upload an Ubuntu ISO, create a guest with the CPUs, RAM and disk they want on the PERC array they already own, attach a NIC, and the page shows them that the guest uplink has link before they press Start. The guest installs, reboots to its disk, gets an address on the customer's network, and they SSH to it from their desk. They can type into it from the browser when SSH is not an option. When the rack loses power the guest comes back on its own. When a new RayNu-V ships they update from the page and roll back from the page. Every one of those actions is in an audit log they can export. Nothing in that paragraph requires COM2.

What the lab box already does of that paragraph (all **lived**, SHAs in the catalog): one EFI on a real R640; install loop to `login:`; Ubuntu 26.04 on a PERC virtual disk; persist across chassis power-off; HTTPS on `:8443`; audit ring with hash chain; a guest virtio NIC that transmits without a watchdog. What is **in flight**: guest frames leaving and returning on LOM port 4 (PR #409), guest address, SSH from another machine, browser console. What is **planned** for S1: signed EFI, in-place update with rollback, operator account and certificate, plaintext boot window closed, uplink discovery and link state on the page, clean shutdown, autostart, host static address and NTP, config store on disk, datastore across the whole VD, FLUSH semantics, Redfish Tier 1 on the page, audit export and persistence, 72-hour iron soak, customer documents.

### Cabling an R640 for Shipment 1

| Jack | Carries | Cable |
|------|---------|-------|
| Dedicated iDRAC | Console (SOL), iDRAC UI, boot media | Yes, or Shared LOM on port 3 |
| LOM port 3 (`01:00.0`) | RayNu-V management page `:8443` | Yes, untagged |
| LOM port 4 (`01:00.1`) | All guest traffic | Yes once a guest has a NIC, untagged |
| 10G ports 1–2 | Nothing in S1 | No |

Separate management and guest ports is also the ESXi best practice. Single-port mode (D13) and operator-chosen port roles (D12) are final-SKU rows.

## Final SKU — every row of the catalog

Areas in [ADR-021 Catalog](adr/ADR-021.md#catalog):

| Area | What it covers |
|------|----------------|
| A | Boot, binary and platform: signed EFI, Secure Boot, TPM measured boot, in-place update, support matrix |
| B | Compute and guest lifecycle: SMP, APIC/MSI, clean shutdown, autostart, snapshots, templates, Windows, cloud-init, hot-add |
| C | Storage: datastore across the VD, FLUSH, config store, NVMe, passthrough, thin, snapshots, export/import, backup, disk health |
| D | Networking: uplink discovery, link state, carrier, DHCP/static, host address/NTP, port roles, single-port mode, VLAN, bonding, 10G, SR-IOV, IPv6 |
| E | Management plane: own certificate, accounts, roles, LDAP/OIDC, tokens, console, OpenAPI, CLI, metrics, alerts, log export |
| F | Hardware and iDRAC: Redfish Tier 1 on the page, SMBIOS, hardware events, PERC health, predictive failure, watchdog, R650/R660 |
| G | Audit and compliance: export, persistence, FinOps metering, SOX/ISO templates, external anchoring |
| H | Reliability, operations, documentation: panic path, 72-hour soak, guest watchdog, customer documents, performance baseline, support policy |
| I | Verification: L2 across the Proven Core, EPT isolation theorem, Kani on every `unsafe`, external review |
| J | Migration from VMware: vCenter read, VMDK convert, config translate, ten guests in one command |
| K | Cluster and elasticity (M9): join, shared storage, live migration, placement, HA |

Outside even the final SKU: a host shell or userspace, a package manager, KVM/Xen/bhyve lineage, ESXi feature parity on day one, Tier 2 iDRAC as a shipping blocker.

## Build order

Waves, not letters: [ADR-021 · Build order](adr/ADR-021.md#build-order-the-rule-behind-decision-5). Wave 0 is the lived base; waves 1–9 are Shipment 1 (wave 9 is the 72-hour iron soak); waves 10–17 are the final SKU; wave V is verification, continuous. Each wave has one iron thread. `./tools/sync-sku-site.sh --next` prints the current wave and what to pick up; the page shows it as **Now building**. Rule for agents: [`.cursor/rules/build-order.mdc`](../.cursor/rules/build-order.mdc).

## Rules for this card

- Edit rows in `docs/adr/ADR-021.md`, then run `./tools/sync-sku-site.sh`. Stage `site/sku.json` with it. Every row must be in exactly one wave; the tool fails otherwise.
- A row becomes **lived** only with R640 evidence (or CI for a host artifact). Latitude and QEMU do not count. The sync tool rejects a lived row with no SHA, marker, tool or document in its note.
- The LOI page ([`site/loi.html`](../site/loi.html)) is a derived view of `site/sku.json`: ADR-021's **Letters** table names the rows Letter A (dedicated box = Shipment 1) and Letter B (RAID fleet = Shipment 1 + C4, C11, D12, D13, F6) need. A letter is ready when every row is lived. No percent, no month; the earlier `docs/loihda.md` scoreboard is retired.
- Rollbacks: M8.9 `v0.1.0-m8-8-ubuntu` (`c3a70e62`); M8.0 `v0.1.0-everest-closed` (`f72b4276`).
